title: de Broglie Matter Waves — Equation, Derivation and Experimental Proof
topicTitle: Elementary idea of quantum mechanical model: de Broglie's wave equation
notes: The derivation of λ = h/mv from the photon equations and the experimental proof — the two parts of de Broglie's idea that complete the main note.

For a photon: $E=h\nu$ and $E=mc^{2}$ (equivalence of energy and mass). Equating: $mc^{2}=h\nu=h\frac{c}{\lambda}$ → $\lambda=\frac{h}{mc}=\frac{h}{p}$. de Broglie's 1924 leap: the same relation must hold for **matter**, so a particle of momentum p = mv has wavelength $\lambda=\frac{h}{mv}$. For accelerated electrons, $\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2meV}}=\frac{12.27}{\sqrt{V}}\ \text{Å}$ (V in volts).
### Why the wave nature is only microscopic

λ ∝ 1/m: a 1 g body at 1 m s⁻¹ has λ ≈ 6.6 × 10⁻³¹ m (undetectable), while a 100 V electron has λ ≈ 1.23 Å — the size of atomic spacings, so crystals diffract electrons. Wave behaviour is not absent for large bodies; it is unobservable.

Electrons accelerated through ≈54 V strike a single nickel crystal; the detector records a maximum at φ = 50°. Bragg's law gives the wavelength: nλ = 2d sin θ with d = 0.091 nm → λ ≈ 0.165 nm; the de Broglie value for 54 V is λ = 12.27/√54 ≈ 1.67 Å = 0.167 nm — agreement within experiment. G. P. Thomson's high-energy electron diffraction through thin films confirmed it independently (both shared the 1937 Nobel Prize).
• Justifies Bohr's quantisation: nλ = 2πr → mvr = nh/2π.
• Basis of the Schrödinger equation and the orbital concept.
• Electron diffraction and the electron microscope (λ ≈ 0.005 nm at 50 kV → atomic resolution); neutron diffraction for structure determination.
• Quantum tunnelling and matter-wave interferometry (atom interferometers, BEC) are direct technologies of matter waves.
confusion: ❌ de Broglie waves travel at the speed of light. ✅ They travel with the particle (v ≪ c); the phase velocity even exceeds c, while the group velocity equals v.
❌ The derivation needs relativistic mass. ✅ For non-relativistic particles λ = h/mv directly; the photon derivation only motivates the form.
❌ Davisson–Germer proved light has particle nature. ✅ It proved *electrons* have wave nature — the converse of the photoelectric effect.

universalFacts: de Broglie received the 1929 Nobel Prize for his 1924 thesis — the first Nobel awarded for a PhD thesis.
λ(54 V electron) ≈ 1.67 Å matched the Davisson–Germer Bragg analysis (d = 0.091 nm, φ = 50°).
Electron microscopes reach ≈0.1 nm resolution because λ(electron) is ~10⁵ times shorter than visible light.
examples: **Problem:** λ of an electron with KE = 13.6 eV. **Solution:** λ = 12.27/√13.6 ≈ 3.33 Å — exactly one circumference of the first Bohr orbit, linking the two topics.
importantNotes: Quote both the general form λ = h/mv and the electron form 12.27/√V Å.

summary: Starting from the photon relations E = hν and E = mc², one obtains λ = h/p; de Broglie's 1924 leap was that the same relation must hold for matter, so a particle of momentum p = mv has wavelength λ = h/mv = h/√(2mKE), and for an electron accelerated through V volts, λ = 12.27/√V Å. Since λ ∝ 1/m, wave behaviour is unobservable for everyday objects (1 g at 1 m s⁻¹ gives λ ≈ 6.6 × 10⁻³¹ m) but dominant for 100 V electrons (λ ≈ 1.23 Å, the scale of atomic spacings). Davisson and Germer (1927) diffracted ≈54 V electrons from a nickel crystal and found λ ≈ 0.165 nm from Bragg's law against 1.67 Å predicted, and G. P. Thomson confirmed it independently. The chemical consequences are the standing-wave justification of Bohr's quantisation (nλ = 2πr), the Schrödinger equation, the orbital, electron microscopy and quantum tunnelling.
importantConcepts: Derivation from the photon relations: mc² = hν = hc/λ gives λ = h/p for matter as well
λ = h/mv = h/p = h/√(2mKE), and for electrons λ = 12.27/√V Å with V in volts
Davisson–Germer (1927): 54 V electrons on nickel, d = 0.091 nm, maximum at φ = 50°, λ ≈ 0.165 nm
Chemical payoff: standing wave nλ = 2πr derives Bohr's mvr = nh/2π
Applications: electron microscope (λ ≈ 0.005 nm at 50 kV), electron and neutron diffraction, tunnelling, atom interferometry
importantStatements: Matter waves travel with the particle; the phase velocity may exceed c while the group velocity equals v.
A heavier body has a shorter de Broglie wavelength, so wave behaviour is a microscopic phenomenon, not an absent one.
The λ = h/mv form is non-relativistic; the photon derivation only motivates the form of the relation.
Davisson–Germer proved that electrons have wave nature — the converse of the photoelectric effect.
For an electron of KE 13.6 eV, λ = 3.33 Å, exactly the circumference of the first Bohr orbit.

keyPoints: Two forms to quote: λ = h/mv for any particle and λ = 12.27/√V Å for electrons.
The 54 V electron result, 1.67 Å predicted against 0.165 nm measured, is the classic verification.
Electron microscopes reach atomic resolution because the electron wavelength is ~10⁵ times shorter than visible light.
nλ = 2πr links this topic directly to Bohr's quantisation condition.
specialNotes: De Broglie's 1929 Nobel Prize was the first ever awarded for a PhD thesis.
Davisson and Germer shared the 1937 Nobel Prize, the year G. P. Thomson's work was recognised too.
Matter waves carry no charge and are not electromagnetic, so they need no medium.
examShortTricks: For electron problems jump straight to λ = 12.27/√V Å; it saves two substitutions.
Order of magnitude check: 1 g at 1 m s⁻¹ gives λ ≈ 10⁻³³ m, so no diffraction is possible.
Mentioning 1927 and nickel crystal is enough to earn the proof mark.
examNotes: Derivation plus the Davisson–Germer evidence is a standard 4–5 mark question.
A 2–3 mark numerical on the wavelength of an accelerated electron is very common.
One-mark items test why macroscopic objects show no wave behaviour.
